claims.claim_text: The indexed William J. Byrne is confirmed as the exact person recorded entering the United States Army as a private on October 20, 1942.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The OSS index and official Army merged record agree on the full printed name and private identifier.
claims.identity_match_assessment: Confirmed by exact private-identifier and exact-name agreement across two official NARA records.
claims.temporal_assessment: The Army record dates entry on October 20, 1942. It does not establish when he joined OSS or whether Army entry immediately preceded OSS service.
claims.match_notes: The full identifier remains private. No common-name biography or employer is assigned.

claims.claim_text: The indexed Stephen Byzek is probably the Stephen J. Byzek identified as an Army captain in a 1957 official Army journal.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: A postwar Army journal names the rare exact-name candidate Stephen J. Byzek as a captain and third-degree judo black belt.
claims.identity_match_assessment: Probable from the distinctive exact first name and rare surname in an official Army source; the source lacks the indexed private identifier, OSS reference, birth date, and Box 99 linkage.
claims.temporal_assessment: The source is from January 1957 and therefore postdates OSS service. It supplies identity context only, not pre-OSS chronology.
claims.match_notes: The postwar captain title is not used to classify wartime commissioned status. Box 99 must confirm the middle initial, birth date, identifier, and service chronology.

claims.claim_text: The indexed George J. Cabaud is identified with high confidence as George John Cabaud, whose 1939-1946 SOE personnel file is held by The National Archives, Kew.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The British National Archives catalogue has a person-specific SOE personnel file for the distinctive exact name George John Cabaud covering 1939-1946.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence from the distinctive surname, exact first name and middle-initial expansion, official person-specific wartime intelligence personnel file, and matching 1939-1946 context.
claims.temporal_assessment: The file's catalogue covering dates overlap OSS operations, but the undigitized description does not establish a specific pre-OSS employer, assignment sequence, or OSS dates.
claims.match_notes: The British file is not digitized. The match remains short of confirmed until Box 100 or HS 9/252/2 supplies a shared identifier or direct OSS linkage.
